```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")

sett_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON("colonial_equatoria_congo_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
summary_cache <- jsonlite::fromJSON("colonial_equatoria_congo_summary_cache.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)

all_keys <- names(sett_raw)
all_entries <- lapply(all_keys, function (k) {
  e <- sett_raw[[k]]
  e$key <- k
  e
})

assign_subregion <- function (e) {
  c <- as.character(e$country)
  lat <- as.numeric(e$coords[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(e$coords[[2]])
  if (c %in% c("Chad", "Niger", "Sudan")) return("aef_chad")
  if (c %in% c("Central African Republic", "South Sudan")) return("aef_ubangi_shari")
  if (identical(c, "Republic of the Congo")) return("aef_middle_congo")
  if (identical(c, "Gabon")) return("aef_gabon")
  if (identical(c, "Equatorial Guinea")) return("spanish_guinea")
  if (c %in% c("Cameroon", "Nigeria")) {
    if (identical(c, "Nigeria") && lat > 12.2) return("aef_chad")
    return("kamerun_mandates")
  }
  if (c %in% c("Burundi", "Rwanda", "Uganda")) return("belgian_congo_orientale_kivu")
  if (c %in% c("Zambia", "United Republic of Tanzania")) return("belgian_congo_kasai_katanga")
  if (identical(c, "Namibia")) return("portuguese_angola_south_huila")
  if (identical(c, "Democratic Republic of the Congo")) {
    if (lon < 21.8 && lat > -8.5) return("belgian_congo_leopoldville_equateur")
    if (lat < -3.8) return("belgian_congo_kasai_katanga")
    return("belgian_congo_orientale_kivu")
  }
  if (identical(c, "Angola")) {
    if (lat > -10.3 && lon < 17.5) return("portuguese_angola_north_cabinda")
    if (lat < -13.6 || (lon > 18.5 && lat < -10.5)) return("portuguese_angola_south_huila")
    return("portuguese_angola_central_benguela")
  }
  "belgian_congo_leopoldville_equateur"
}

iso3_map <- c(
  "Angola" = "AGO",
  "Burundi" = "BDI",
  "Cameroon" = "CMR",
  "Central African Republic" = "CAF",
  "Chad" = "TCD",
  "Democratic Republic of the Congo" = "COD",
  "Equatorial Guinea" = "GNQ",
  "Gabon" = "GAB",
  "Namibia" = "NAM",
  "Niger" = "NER",
  "Nigeria" = "NGA",
  "Republic of the Congo" = "COG",
  "Rwanda" = "RWA",
  "South Sudan" = "SSD",
  "Sudan" = "SDN",
  "Uganda" = "UGA",
  "United Republic of Tanzania" = "TZA",
  "Zambia" = "ZMB"
)

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", yrs[i_pk], "AD)")
}

subregion_order <- c(
  "aef_chad",
  "aef_ubangi_shari",
  "aef_middle_congo",
  "aef_gabon",
  "kamerun_mandates",
  "spanish_guinea",
  "belgian_congo_leopoldville_equateur",
  "belgian_congo_orientale_kivu",
  "belgian_congo_kasai_katanga",
  "portuguese_angola_north_cabinda",
  "portuguese_angola_central_benguela",
  "portuguese_angola_south_huila"
)

sub_by_id <- setNames(summary_cache$subregions, vapply(summary_cache$subregions, function (x) x$id, character(1)))

entry_sub_ids <- vapply(all_entries, assign_subregion, character(1))

zone_entries <- setNames(lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- all_entries[entry_sub_ids == sid]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
}), subregion_order)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- viscount_iso3(e$country)
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Location = loc_str,
      `1885AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1885),
      `1900AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1900),
      `1930AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1930),
      `1950AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1950),
      `1960AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1960),
      `1970AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1970),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1880, 1900, 1930, 1950, 1960, 1970)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and colonial-era population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed urban settlements and metropolitan agglomerations across `r viscount_fmt_number(length(summary_cache$countries), 0L)` countries between 1880AD and 1975AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate colonial stations, mining centres, river ports and provincial capitals (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` excluded), the retained entries span 12 colonial sub-regions across French Equatorial Africa, German and Mandate Cameroon, Spanish Guinea, the Belgian Congo and Portuguese Angola. Active interpolated entries rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1880"]], 0L)` settlements at 1880AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1900"]], 0L)` at 1900AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1930"]], 0L)` at 1930AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1950"]], 0L)` at 1950AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1960"]], 0L)` at 1960AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1970"]], 0L)` at 1970AD, tracing urban expansion from small concession posts to Kinshasa (1,29M), Luanda (475,3k), Lubumbashi (318k), Brazzaville (290k), Douala (289,1k agglomeration) and Bangui (279,8k).

```{r fig1-md-only, results='asis'}

  viscount_figure(
    "figures/fig_01_map.png",
    "Spatial distribution of 2.178 individually assessed settlements across 18 countries spanning twelve colonial sub-regions from 1880AD to 1975AD.",
    "fig:hero-settlements-equatoria"
  )
}
```

# Background

Documenting urban growth across colonial Equatorial and West-Central Africa requires harmonising heterogeneous administrative enumerations across five imperial statistical traditions [@Starr1911TheCongo; @AEFAnnuaire1950; @Angola1940Censo]. Belgian annual reports (*Rapports Annuels sur l'Administration de la Colonie du Congo Belge*) and the 1955-1957AD demographic sample survey tracked *centres extra-coutumiers* and copperbelt labour towns in detail [@CongoBelge1958Enquete; @Depaepe2017ColonialEducation], whereas French Equatorial Africa's statistical yearbooks and Mandate Cameroon censuses separated European and African *commune* rolls [@AEFAnnuaire1950; @Gouellain1975Douala]. Portuguese Angolan censuses beginning in 1940AD and early post-independence national censuses provide late-colonial municipal totals alongside Africapolis metropolitan boundaries from 1950AD onward [@Angola1940Censo; @Rodrigues2022WhenModern; @Oula2024CrossPerspective].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Sub-Regional Partition

Candidate urban sites were screened from official territorial census tables, missionary and colonial expedition accounts and Africapolis urban-extent inventories [@AEFAnnuaire1950; @CongoBelge1958Enquete; @Angola1940Censo; @Gouellain1975Douala]. Within the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² domain bounded by geoBoundaries national polygons [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate alias records were removed, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` chronological observations. Each entry is assigned to one of 12 colonial sub-regions, grouping 37 immediate cross-border catchment towns in Nigeria, Zambia, Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan, Niger and Tanzania into their adjoining sub-region [@Tsafack2022CameroonEquatorial; @Silva2020TheFormal].

## Site-Specific Population Estimation and Spatial Scope

Of the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries, `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$city_proper, 0L)` record municipal city-proper populations and `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$metro, 0L)` trace continuous urban agglomerations labelled explicitly as "(Agglomeration)" in the tables below. Tables 1 to 12 report linearly interpolated populations at six colonial benchmarks (1885AD, 1900AD, 1930AD, 1950AD, 1960AD and 1970AD) together with each site's observed peak population and peak date, marking years outside an entry's attested span with a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Rank-size regression on peak populations over the upper half (n=`r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$rank_size$n_fit, 0L)`) of the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements yields $q = `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$rank_size$zipf_q, 2L)`$ ($R^2 = `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$rank_size$r2, 2L)`$), closely matching the 343 spatially deduplicated entries plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank} ($q = 0,93$, $R^2 = 0,99$). Separate municipal and agglomeration rows preserve consistency between pre-1950AD colonial township counts and post-1950AD metropolitan growth [@Rodrigues2022WhenModern; @Gouellain1975Douala].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 343 spatially deduplicated settlements (q = 0,93, R² = 0,99) and top ten sub-regional densities in 1975AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## French Equatorial Africa: Colony of Chad

Table \ref{tab:sub-chad} compiles `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["aef_chad"]]), 0L)` settlements across Chad and the bordering Lake Chad and Darfur fringes, led by Fort-Lamy/Ndjamena (148,9k agglomeration), Sarh (43,7k), Moundou (39,6k) and Abéché (27,3k), reflecting the early decline of Wadai's capital followed by mid-century cotton-zone urbanisation [@AEFAnnuaire1950].

```{r tab-chad, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["aef_chad"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the AEF Colony of Chad and Lake Chad borderlands (1885AD to 1970AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-chad")
)
```

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this urban gazetteer. First, `r viscount_fmt_number(sum(vapply(all_entries, function (x) length(x$population) == 1L, logical(1))), 0L)` of the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements hold a single dated population observation, so benchmark columns outside their observed date display a hyphen (-). Second, early colonial urban enumerations before 1930AD frequently covered only European residents and taxed male workers, understating African suburban compounds around Libreville, Bangui, Luanda and Léopoldville [@Starr1911TheCongo; @AEFAnnuaire1950; @Angola1940Censo]. Third, both city-proper and post-1950AD agglomeration rows appear for 14 major capitals and ports; users aggregating regional urban totals must select one spatial scope per city rather than summing both rows.

# Conclusion

Taken together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements document the rise of colonial port capitals, riverine administrative seats, copperbelt mining cities and late-colonial metropolitan agglomerations across 18 countries in Equatorial and West-Central Africa between 1880AD and 1975AD.

# Appendix

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums the assessed site counts and combined interpolated site populations across all 12 sub-regions from 1880AD to 1970AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[sid]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(sub_by_id[[sid]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1880AD` = sums[["1880"]],
    `1900AD` = sums[["1900"]],
    `1930AD` = sums[["1930"]],
    `1950AD` = sums[["1950"]],
    `1960AD` = sums[["1960"]],
    `1970AD` = sums[["1970"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Subregions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1880AD` = tot_sums[["1880"]],
  `1900AD` = tot_sums[["1900"]],
  `1930AD` = tot_sums[["1930"]],
  `1950AD` = tot_sums[["1950"]],
  `1960AD` = tot_sums[["1960"]],
  `1970AD` = tot_sums[["1970"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated populations across twelve colonial sub-regions from 1880AD to 1970AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```

Linear interpolation is bounded strictly between each settlement's earliest and latest observed dates; pre-observation and post-observation benchmarks are marked with a hyphen (-). Dual municipal and agglomeration entries exist for 14 major urban centres and should not be summed simultaneously when calculating city-proper urban totals.
